title: Crochet for left-handed makers
subtitle: How left-handed crochet differs from right-handed and how to adapt patterns
excerpt: Left-handed crochet holds the hook in the left hand and the working yarn in the right, which is the mirror image of right-handed crochet. Most instructions and diagrams are written for right-handed makers. Left-handed crocheters who follow right-handed diagrams produce the same fabric with the same structure, but the direction of travel is reversed. Understanding the differences makes it possible to follow any pattern correctly.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book (Storey Publishing). Pauline Turner, How to Crochet (HarperCollins).

glossaryTerms.definition: Left-handed crochet worked as a precise mirror of right-handed crochet. The hook is held in the left hand and the work travels from left to right (the reverse of right-handed crochet). The finished fabric is structurally identical.

The direction in which the work progresses across a row. Right-handed crochet works from right to left; left-handed crochet works from left to right. When a pattern says 'work to the end of the row,' the direction reverses for left-handed crocheters but the stitch count and result are the same.

Direction of travel: each row moves from left to right (the opposite of right-handed). When turning at the end of a row, the work turns in the same physical manner as for right-handed crochet, just in the opposite horizontal direction.

Diagrams: right-handed crochet diagrams are read from right to left for the first row. Left-handed crocheters read the same diagram from left to right. The stitches within the diagram remain the same symbols and mean the same thing.

Left/right edge instructions: swap the words left and right in any edge instruction. Work decreases at your right edge when the pattern says right edge. The finished piece looks the same from either maker.

Twist in stitches: the natural twist direction of the stitch may vary slightly. If a stitch looks twisted compared to a right-handed sample, try inserting the hook from the front or back of the stitch to reverse the twist until the stitch appears flat.
Replace any instruction that says "right edge" with "left edge" and vice versa. Stitch counts and the number of stitches before and after shaping remain the same.
For garments shaped at both edges the same way (raglan, side shaping), no change is needed. Both edges get the same treatment and the reversal makes no difference to the finished piece.

For asymmetric pieces (a left sleeve cap is different from a right sleeve cap), swap the two pieces: work the piece labelled "left sleeve" for the right and vice versa. The finished sleeves will be correct for the left-handed maker's arms.

items.symptom: The stitches look twisted compared to right-handed samples
items.cause: The hook is going into the stitch from the wrong angle, causing the yarn wrap to twist the stitch head.
items.fix: Try inserting the hook from the back of the stitch to the front rather than front to back (or vice versa) and see which produces an untwisted stitch head. The correct entry direction is the one that makes the finished stitch look like the pattern photo.

items.symptom: A colour pattern is mirrored relative to the pattern photo
items.cause: In colourwork worked flat, the left-handed direction of travel reverses the visual direction of the pattern in each row.
items.fix: For colourwork charts, read the chart from left to right on right-side rows (the reverse of right-handed). On wrong-side rows, read from right to left. The chart result will match the pattern photo.

content.text: Work a simple 20-stitch, 10-row double crochet swatch using a standard right-handed pattern, reading all instructions as written. Compare the finished swatch to the right-handed version. They will be identical in structure; the only difference is which hand the hook is in. This confirms that left-handed crocheters can follow any pattern without special left-handed instructions.
